classification.classification_note: The staged crash is a stack-use-after-scope read. `xmlEscapeText()` stores a pointer to block-local stack `tempBuf` in `repl`, the branch ends, and `memcpy(out, repl, replSize)` later reads through that expired stack address.

bug_description.original: Stack-use-after-scope in xmlEscapeText (xmlIO.c): xmlEscapeText uses data from a stack-allocated temporary buffer after that buffer's lifetime ends, causing a read of stale stack memory (observed via a memcpy). This is reachable via node string handling / element validation (xmlNodeListGetStringInternal -> xmlValidateElement) and can lead to crashes or other memory-corruption impacts when parsing crafted XML.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The 43-byte witness uses libxml2's `fuzz/valid` entity-container format: after the initial 8-byte option and failure fields plus an empty URL string terminated by `\\n`, the main entity bytes are `<!DOCTYPE[<!ATTLISTa p  ID '\xFF' \xFF<a`. Stage 01 proves `xmlCtxtReadMemory()` accepts that entity (`doc != NULL`) and post-parse DTD validation reaches `xmlValidateElement()`. During attribute validation, `xmlNodeListGetString(doc, attr->children, 0)` enables escaping, sets `XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII`, and routes attacker-derived non-ASCII text into `xmlEscapeText()`. In the `offset < 0` branch, vulnerable code declares block-local `char tempBuf[12]`, writes the replacement character reference into it, and stores `repl = tempBuf`. When that branch ends, `tempBuf` is out of scope but `repl` is still used by `memcpy(out, repl, replSize)` at `xmlIO.c:362`. AddressSanitizer reports a stack-use-after-scope read there and identifies `tempBuf` at line 318 as the poisoned stack object. The fix moves `tempBuf` to the top of the loop so the later copy still points to live stack storage.

source.description: First project-side statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-derived parsed document state and requests escaped serialization of an attribute child list. Passing `0` as `inLine` is what sends the data into the escaping logic that eventually reaches `xmlEscapeText()`.
source.value_from: The `fuzz/valid` witness stores an empty main URL and then the main-entity bytes `<!DOCTYPE[<!ATTLISTa p  ID '\xFF' \xFF<a` after the `\\n` separator. Stage 01's reproduced run proves `xmlCtxtReadMemory()` returned `doc != NULL` and `xmlCtxtValidateDocument()` reached `xmlValidateElement()`, so `attr->children` here is parsed document state derived from attacker-controlled bytes.

sink.description: ASan sink. `repl` still points to expired stack `tempBuf`, so this copy reads the serialized replacement bytes from out-of-scope stack storage.

root_cause.description: Patch-relevant lifetime bug. `tempBuf` is declared only inside the `offset < 0` branch, so its lifetime ends at that branch's closing brace even though later code still uses a pointer derived from it. The fix moves this declaration to the top of the loop body.
root_cause.note: The unsafe alias is created in the next step when `repl = tempBuf`, but the missing lifetime obligation originates from this too-narrow scope.

tainted_value_origin.code:
doc = xmlCtxtReadMemory(ctxt, docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL,
                                opts & ~XML_PARSE_DTDVALID);
tainted_value_origin.description: The harness passes the main entity extracted from the fuzz container into libxml2's XML parser, materializing the `doc` whose attribute child nodes later feed `xmlValidateElement()` and `xmlEscapeText()`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness passed libxml2's XML parser in the post-validation path, so the harness entered document validation with a non-null parsed `doc`.

coarse_trace.summary: The witness's main entity is accepted by `xmlCtxtReadMemory()`, and the post-validation path calls `xmlCtxtValidateDocument()` on the resulting `doc`.
While validating parsed element attributes, libxml2 serializes an attacker-derived attribute child list with `xmlNodeListGetString(doc, attr->children, 0)`.
The string wrapper turns on escaping and non-ASCII handling, then passes text-node content into `xmlEscapeText()`.
The non-ASCII branch builds a replacement string in block-local `tempBuf`, leaves `repl` pointing at that stack buffer after the branch ends, and `memcpy()` then reads from the expired buffer.

fine_trace.note: Source. Attribute validation consumes attacker-derived `attr->children` from the accepted document and requests non-inline serialization by passing `inLine == 0`.

Because step 1 passed `inLine == 0`, the wrapper enables escaping. On this witness the document is not HTML and has no stored encoding declaration, so `XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII` is set; since the list belongs to an attribute, `XML_ESCAPE_ATTR` is also added.
The internal serializer reaches a text-node child with non-null content and, because escaping is enabled, passes that attacker-derived byte string and the flags from step 2 into `xmlEscapeText()`.

While scanning `node->content`, the current byte is non-ASCII and step 2 supplied `XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII`, so the inner loop breaks without setting an escape-table offset. `offset` therefore stays `-1`, selecting the UTF-8/char-ref branch.
Root cause. The `offset < 0` branch allocates the replacement buffer on the stack with lifetime limited to this `else` block.

The branch converts the current non-ASCII byte sequence into a replacement character reference inside `tempBuf`, records the produced length in `replSize`, and makes `repl` alias that block-local buffer.

Reaching the next statement means control has left the `else` block, so `tempBuf` is already out of scope. The pointer and length from step 6 remain unchanged, leaving `repl` as a stale alias to expired stack storage.

Sink. The copy reads `replSize` bytes from `repl` after step 7 left it pointing to out-of-scope `tempBuf`. Stage 01's ASan trace reports stack-use-after-scope here and names `tempBuf` at line 318 as the poisoned stack object.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan's frame report identifies stack object `tempBuf` at `xmlEscapeText()` line 318, and step 5 is that same declaration whose scope ends before step 8 reads through `repl`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved reproduced trace reports `READ of size 8` at `xmlIO.c:362`; the reference crash trace from the dataset reports the same sink and poisoned object with `READ of size 7` on a nearby build. Both artifacts agree on the vulnerable source location and lifetime failure.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz/valid entity-container
format.contract: The witness must follow libxml2's fuzz-entity container format: 8 leading option/failure bytes, then an empty main-URL string terminated by `\\n`, then the exact main-entity bytes `<!DOCTYPE[<!ATTLISTa p  ID '\xFF' \xFF<a`. On the witnessed path those bytes must parse to `doc != NULL` and later present a non-ASCII attribute-child byte during `xmlCtxtValidateDocument()`, so `xmlNodeListGetString(..., 0)` enables `XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII` and `xmlEscapeText()` takes the block-local `tempBuf` branch.
